3) Categories of Procedures
General procedure classification: generally follows the test procedures listed below.

Procedure I — Functional shock. Used to evaluate the working state of the equipment (including machine tools, electrical, air pressure, hydraulic, and electrical) subjected to shock testing, to assess the equipment's shock resistance performance and function consistency. It is generally required that the equipment be in working condition during the shock application period and to be able to identify those nearby functional areas that may not be damaged by shock.

Procedure II — Packaged equipment, specifically freight-packaged equipment. It verifies that the minimum outer edge of the shock capacity is set at the level to which the packaging reduces it. Due to the packaging equipment not being designed for evaluation, the precise calibration level value is not required to be met by the packaging equipment, and the tail end impact damping platform, etc., in the testing.

Procedure III — Fragility. Used to determine the fragility of the equipment as a guide, an approach for the design of new equipment to provide specifications. The procedure is used to confirm the equipment's temporary shock conditions. In the test, when the shock conditions on the equipment's structural strength are not sufficient to meet requirements, it is desired to achieve better actual level capability. The procedure should be used at an appropriate level of environmental temperature.
